GPX Files: The Touring Rider's Route Format

GPX (GPS Exchange Format) files are the universal language of motorcycle route sharing. A GPX file contains a series of GPS coordinates that describe a route — download one, load it on your device, and follow it turn by turn. If you're not using GPX files for your touring, you're missing out on thousands of curated routes shared by riders who know the best roads.

What Is a GPX File?

A GPX file is a simple text file containing latitude and longitude coordinates that trace a route. It can include:

  • Routes: A planned path from A to B with waypoints
  • Tracks: A recorded journey showing exactly where someone rode
  • Waypoints: Individual points of interest (viewpoints, fuel stops, cafes)

The beauty of GPX is its universality — the same file works on Garmin, TomTom, Google Maps, and every major navigation app.

Where to Find GPX Routes

  • VisorUp: Our route planner exports GPX files for all our curated UK motorcycle routes.
  • Kurviger: A motorcycle-specific routing platform with GPX export and a huge library of community routes.
  • Calimoto: Motorcycle route app with GPX import/export and thousands of shared routes.
  • Wikiloc: Outdoor route sharing platform with a motorcycle category.
  • Facebook groups: UK motorcycle touring groups regularly share GPX files of recommended routes.
  • Forum posts: UKGSer, Adventure Bike Rider, and other forums have extensive route databases.

How to Create Your Own GPX Files

Planning your own route and exporting it as GPX is straightforward:

  • Google Maps: Plot your route, then use a converter tool (gpsvisualizer.com) to export as GPX.
  • Kurviger.com: Purpose-built for motorcycle routes. Plot waypoints, set preferences (avoid motorways, prefer curvy roads), export as GPX.
  • Basecamp (Garmin): Free software for Garmin GPS users. Create routes on your computer and transfer to your device.
  • RideWithGPS: Online route planner with excellent map layers and GPX export.

Loading GPX Files on Your Device

On a Garmin GPS:

  • Connect your GPS via USB
  • Copy the GPX file to the Garmin > NewFiles folder
  • Disconnect and restart — the route appears in your saved trips

On a smartphone (Kurviger/Calimoto):

  • Download the GPX file to your phone
  • Open the app and select "Import Route" or "Open GPX"
  • The route loads and you can follow it with turn-by-turn navigation

On Google Maps:

  • Upload the GPX file to Google My Maps (mymaps.google.com)
  • View the route overlaid on Google Maps
  • Note: Google Maps doesn't natively import GPX — you need My Maps as an intermediary
Always preview a GPX route before riding it. Someone else's idea of a great road might include tracks, fords, or roads unsuitable for your bike. Load it up, zoom in on the map, and check it looks sensible before committing.

Tips for Using GPX on Tour

  • Download the GPX file and test it on your device before departure
  • Set your navigation to follow the GPX route, not recalculate to the shortest path
  • Use "track" mode rather than "route" mode if your device supports it — tracks follow the exact path rather than letting the GPS interpret it
  • Carry multiple day routes as separate GPX files for easy daily loading
  • Share your planned GPX with your safety contact

GPX files are the key to discovering Britain's best motorcycle roads without spending hours planning. Download, load, ride, enjoy. keyTakeaways: A GPX file stores routes, tracks and waypoints in a universal format readable by most GPS units and apps.
Find ready-made routes on VisorUp, Kurviger, Calimoto, Wikiloc, forums and Facebook groups.
Create your own on Kurviger, Basecamp, RideWithGPS or by exporting from Google Maps.
Load GPX onto a Garmin via the Basecamp software or the GPX folder, or import directly into Kurviger/Calimoto on a phone.
Always download offline maps to back up GPX navigation where there is no signal.

faq.a: GPX (GPS Exchange Format) is a universal file type for storing navigation data. It can contain routes, which are waypoints joined by roads and recalculated by your device, tracks, which are fixed breadcrumb trails of points from a recorded ride, and waypoints, which mark single locations such as fuel stops or viewpoints. Almost every GPS unit and navigation app can read GPX.

faq.q: How do I load a GPX file onto a Garmin?
faq.a: The simplest way is through Garmin BaseCamp: import the GPX into BaseCamp, then transfer the route to your connected device. Alternatively, connect the Garmin to your computer, open its storage, and copy the GPX file into the GPX folder. On the device, the route then appears under saved routes or trips ready to follow.

faq.q: Can I use GPX files on my phone?
faq.a: Yes. Apps such as Kurviger and Calimoto let you import a GPX file directly and navigate turn by turn, which is ideal for scenic routing. You can also open GPX in mapping apps for offline use. Always download offline maps first, because much of touring Britain has no mobile signal and online-only navigation will fail.

faq.q: How do I create my own GPX route?
faq.a: Use a route planner such as Kurviger.com, RideWithGPS or Garmin BaseCamp to plot your waypoints, favouring twisty roads, then export the result as a GPX file. You can also build a route in Google Maps and export it. Save the file to your phone or GPS, and test it on a short local ride before committing to a full tour.
